entities.summary: Fortún Ximénez Bertandoña, a Spanish sailor of Basque origin, led a mutiny during an early expedition along the Pacific Coast of Mexico in 1532, becoming the first European known to have landed in the Baja California peninsula. This event marked a pivotal moment in the history of European exploration and the colonization of the Americas. The mutiny also had significant consequences for the indigenous populations of the region, who were affected by the arrival of European settlers and the subsequent exploitation of their resources. Fortún Ximénez's journey has been documented by historians as a testament to the bravery and determination of early Spanish explorers. His legacy continues to be studied by scholars today as a key moment in the development of European maritime power.
